correctness.rationale: For a selected nonbridge vertex on a clique side of order \(m\), the defining inequality is exactly \(k-1\ge m-k\), hence \(k\ge h_m\). For a selected bridge endpoint it is \(k-1+\beta\ge m-k+1-\beta\), hence \(k+\beta\ge g_m\). If a set meets both clique sides, induced connectedness forces both bridge endpoints, after which the nonbridge thresholds suffice. These disjoint cases prove the polynomial for all \(r,s\ge3\). Exhaustive enumeration for every \(3\le r,s\le7\) matched all 275 checked coefficients and all minimum exponents.

value.rationale: Dumbbell graphs are a canonical cut-edge family joining two maximally dense blocks. The result gives every coefficient of the standard strong alliance polynomial, not only a minimum number, and isolates a genuine bridge effect: an endpoint selected without the opposite endpoint has the stricter threshold \(g_m\), while cross-clique connected alliances factor through forced selection of both bridge endpoints. The complete unimodality classification also turns the family into an infinite canonical source of non-unimodal strong alliance polynomials, directly addressing a structural theme of the founding paper. This is a natural exact family missing from the exact-family lists inspected.
